reason: Decompose a C++ expression parser for Proof #3. Lexer -> parser -> AST -> evaluator -> REPL pipeline, deliberately small but complete, in a non-Python language (claim C3). Real constraints: precedence climbing with right-associative exponent, unary operators, function calls with arity checks, scientific-notation numbers, positioned error reporting, and a full unit+CLI test harness under plain make (claim C1). 17 tasks across foundation/frontend/runtime/tests/app/docs subsystems with a 19-edge dependency DAG.

events.title: Project skeleton and layout
events.description: Create examples/expr-parser layout: src/ for implementation, include/expr/ for headers, tests/ for test sources. Add .gitignore ignoring build artifacts (expr, expr_tests, *.o). Add an empty src/main.cpp that returns 0 (replaced by the REPL task later).
acceptance: src/main.cpp exists and compiles to a runnable binary

events.title: Makefile build/test/clean
events.description: Write Makefile: CXX=g++, CXXFLAGS=-std=c++14 -Wall -Wextra. Targets: all (build src/*.cpp into ./expr), test (build and run ./expr_tests from tests/*.cpp + src/*.cpp, exit nonzero on failure), clean (remove expr, expr_tests, *.o). No cmake required.
acceptance: make test runs the test binary

events.title: Token kind enum and Token struct
events.description: include/expr/token.h: enum class TokenKind { Number, Identifier, Plus, Minus, Star, Slash, Caret, Percent, LParen, RParen, Comma, End, Error }; struct Token { TokenKind kind; std::string text; size_t pos; }; plus const char* token_kind_name(TokenKind) for diagnostics.
acceptance: token_kind_name returns a readable string for every kind

events.title: ParseError and EvalError with positions
events.description: include/expr/error.h: struct ParseError { std::string message; size_t pos; }; struct EvalError { std::string message; }; both derive from std::exception. Helper std::string render_error(const std::string& source, const ParseError& e) producing 'message\n<source>\n  ^ (at column N)' so errors point at the offending character.
acceptance: render_error includes the caret line and column number

events.title: Lexer with numbers, identifiers, operators, errors
events.description: src/lexer.cpp + include/expr/lexer.h: std::vector<Token> lex(const std::string& src). Skip whitespace. Numbers: integers, decimals (1.5), exponent notation (1e3, 2.5e-2). Identifiers [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*. Operators: + - * / ^ % ( ) ,. Unknown character -> TokenKind::Error token with position (do not throw; the parser decides). Input ends with an End token at src.size().
acceptance: lex("2+3*4") yields Number Plus Number Star Number End
lex("1e3") yields a single Number token with text "1e3"
lex("2$3") yields an Error token at the position of '$'

events.title: Lexer unit tests
events.description: tests/lexer_tests.cpp: table-driven checks. Cover: basic ops, decimals, exponent notation (1e3, 2.5e-2), identifiers, mixed whitespace, unknown char error, empty input (End only). Print 'lexer tests: N passed' on success; exit nonzero on any failure.
acceptance: test binary reports a clear pass/fail summary

events.title: AST node definitions
events.description: include/expr/ast.h: struct Node { enum Kind { Number, Variable, Unary, Binary, Call } kind; double number; std::string name; char op; std::shared_ptr<Node> left, right; std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Node>> args; }; plus factory helpers: make_number(double), make_variable(std::string), make_unary(char, node), make_binary(char, l, r), make_call(name, args). Use std::shared_ptr (C++14; no std::variant on GCC 6).
acceptance: factory helpers construct the right node kinds

events.title: Precedence-climbing parser
events.description: src/parser.cpp + include/expr/parser.h: std::shared_ptr<Node> parse(const std::vector<Token>& tokens) (throws ParseError). Precedence: lowest + - (left assoc), then * / % (left assoc), then ^ (RIGHT assoc), unary - and + bind tighter than * / but looser than ^ (so -2^2 == -(2^2) == -4). Parentheses group. Identifier followed by '(' is a function call with comma-separated arguments (allow empty call? no - at least one arg). Trailing tokens after a complete expression are a ParseError. ')' with no matching '(' is a ParseError. Track current token index; report positions from tokens.
acceptance: dangling ')' or trailing garbage throws ParseError with position

events.title: Parser unit tests
events.description: tests/parser_tests.cpp: build token vectors via lex and check AST shapes. Cases: precedence (2+3*4), left associativity (10-3-2 == (10-3)-2), right associativity (2^3^2), unary minus on numbers and on parens (-(2+3)), function calls (sin(x), pow(2,3)), parenthesized grouping, error cases (")", "2+", "2 3" trailing, missing closing paren). Use a small AST-shape printer for assertions. Exit nonzero on any failure.

events.title: Variable context and builtin functions
events.description: include/expr/context.h + src/context.cpp: class Context { double& operator[](std::string); bool has(name) const; }; builtins table: sin cos tan asin acos atan sqrt cbrt abs log log10 exp floor ceil round; constants pi and e seeded. Table maps name -> double(*)(double).
acceptance: builtin function table contains at least 12 math functions

events.title: Evaluator over the AST
events.description: src/evaluator.cpp + include/expr/evaluator.h: double eval(const std::shared_ptr<Node>&, const Context&) (throws EvalError). Number -> value. Variable -> lookup, unknown variable throws EvalError. Unary -/+ -> negate/identity. Binary: + - * / % ^ with double math (fmod for %, pow for ^). Division by zero throws EvalError('division by zero'). Call: look up builtin, unknown function throws EvalError, call with the argument evaluated. No arity>1 builtins needed except pow handled as n-ary? Keep single-arg builtins; pow(2,3) support: special-case pow with two args in evaluator.

events.title: Evaluator pipeline tests
events.description: tests/evaluator_tests.cpp: full pipeline lex->parse->eval. Cases: 2+2, 10-3-2, 3*4+5, 2^10, 2^3^2, sqrt(9), abs(-4), sin(0), pi*2, x*2 with Context x=21 -> 42, 1/0 throws, 5%2 == 1, 2+3*4 == 14, -2^2 == -4, pow(2,3) == 8. Exit nonzero on any failure.
acceptance: all pipeline cases evaluate to expected values

events.title: AST pretty printer
events.description: include/expr/print.h + src/print.cpp: std::string print_ast(const std::shared_ptr<Node>&) producing S-expression-ish output: Number(n), Variable(name), Unary(op expr), Binary(op l r), Call(name args...). Used by parser tests and the REPL debug command.
acceptance: print_ast handles Call and Unary nodes

events.title: REPL and single-shot CLI
events.description: Replace src/main.cpp with the real CLI. Modes: (a) argv expression mode: ./expr "2+3" prints the result and exits 0; parse/eval errors print the rendered error to stderr and exit 1. (b) interactive REPL when no args: prompt '> ', read a line, lex/parse/eval, print the result (with up to 12 significant digits), print rendered errors and continue; 'quit' or EOF exits 0. Hidden command ':ast <expr>' prints the AST via print_ast.
acceptance: ./expr "1/0" prints error to stderr and exits 1
./expr "2+" prints a positioned parse error and exits 1
REPL evaluates and exits on quit/EOF

events.title: CLI end-to-end tests
events.description: tests/cli_tests.cpp: a driver that runs the built ./expr binary with system() or fork/exec: asserts "2+3" -> stdout "5", "10-3-2" -> "5", "1/0" -> nonzero exit + stderr contains 'division by zero', "2+" -> nonzero exit + stderr contains 'column', "pi" -> 3.14159...; also REPL via piped stdin ("2+3\nquit\n" -> "5"). Print 'cli tests: N passed'.
acceptance: single-shot mode outputs correct values and exit codes

events.title: Edge-case stress tests
events.description: tests/edge_cases.cpp: deep nesting (50 nested parens), long chains (1+2+...+100 == 5050), whitespace-heavy input, empty input error, unary chains (---5 == -5), 5*-3, 1e-3, scientific with negative exponent, % with negatives (fmod semantics), sqrt(-1) -> NaN handling (evaluate, don't crash), very large numbers (1e308), function calls in expressions (sin(0)+cos(0) == 1).
acceptance: all stress cases produce correct values or clean errors
